title: Crispy Chickpea Bowls with Lemony Yogurt (stovetop)
source: adapted from [Warm Chickpea Bowls With Lemony Yogurt — Bon Appétit, Andy Baraghani](https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/warm-chickpea-bowls-with-lemony-yogurt) (4.8★/110)

bowls.name: Lemony yogurt
bowls.arrowText: stirred at step 2, → bowls at step 7
items: ¾ cup plain Greek yogurt
1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice

bowls.name: Lemony salad
bowls.arrowText: tossed at step 2, → on top at step 7
items: ½ cucumber, thinly sliced
a little thin-sliced onion
big handful chopped parsley
3 Tbsp fresh lemon juice

bowls.name: Chickpeas
items: 1 15-oz can chickpeas (no-salt-added), rinsed and patted very dry

bowls.name: Bloom
bowls.arrowText: → cleared spot in pan at step 5
items: 1 garlic clove, grated
1½ tsp ground cumin (a little extra stands in for the original's coriander)

bowls.name: Kale
items: 1 small bunch kale, stems stripped, torn large

stationExtras.label: Stove-side
items: ~3 Tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided (2 Tbsp at step 3, a little at step 5, thread to finish)
lime squeeze to finish
black pepper

steps.text: **Mise — no heat (~15 min).** Work the bowl map above — everything prepped and beside the stove before heat goes on. **Reset before ignition:** dump the garbage bowl, wash knife & board, wipe the counter. Once the burner clicks on, the knife is done.
steps.leadIn: Mise — no heat (~15 min).

steps.text: **Sauces — no heat (~2 min).** Stir Bowl ① (yogurt + lemon). Toss Bowl ② (cucumber, onion, parsley + lemon).
steps.leadIn: Sauces — no heat (~2 min).

steps.text: **Preheat — MEDIUM-HIGH (~2 min).** Empty stainless pan until a water drop skates; add 2 Tbsp olive oil, swirl to a shimmer.
steps.leadIn: Preheat — MEDIUM-HIGH (~2 min).

steps.text: **Crisp the chickpeas — stay on MEDIUM-HIGH (8–10 min).** Bowl ③ in a single layer; leave 2–3 min between stirs. Done when: deep golden, skins splitting, rattly-sounding. *Dead minutes: rinse the colander and board, set out the 2 serving bowls.*
steps.leadIn: Crisp the chickpeas — stay on MEDIUM-HIGH (8–10 min).

steps.text: **Bloom — drop to MEDIUM (30–45 sec).** Bowl ④ (cumin + garlic) in a little oil in a cleared spot until fragrant, then stir through (garlic goes in late so it doesn't burn).
steps.leadIn: Bloom — drop to MEDIUM (30–45 sec).

steps.text: **Kale — stay on MEDIUM (2–3 min).** Bowl ⑤ in; toss until wilted with crisp edges. **OFF HEAT**, squeeze of lime.
steps.leadIn: Kale — stay on MEDIUM (2–3 min).

steps.text: **Plate — no heat.** Yogurt down, chickpea-kale over, lemony salad on top, thread of olive oil.
steps.leadIn: Plate — no heat.

title: Turkey Marinara Skillet (jar-stretch, low-sodium)
source: Adapted from "Amazing Ground Turkey Tomato Sauce" (Allrecipes, 4.6★) — https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/236982/amazing-ground-turkey-tomato-sauce/

bowls.name: Sofrito
items: ½ yellow onion, chopped
2 garlic cloves, minced

bowls.name: Spices
bowls.arrowText: → pan at step 5, on the aromatics
items: 1 tsp dried oregano
¼ tsp chili flakes
generous black pepper

bowls.name: Tomatoes
items: 1 cup jarred marinara (the open jar — measure it, don't pour free)
1 can (14.5 oz) no-salt-added tomatoes, hand-crushed

bowls.name: Finish
items: 2 tbsp part-skim ricotta per bowl
2 tbsp chopped parsley
splash balsamic (the balance move, step 8)

stationExtras.label: Stove-side
items: 1½ tbsp olive oil
1 lb 93% ground turkey (straight from fridge pack)
the cooked pasta + a splash of water to loosen

steps.text: **Mise — set the station (no heat, ~2 min).** Garbage bowl, damp towel under board, hand towel, landing plate. Read the steps through. Once the burner clicks on, the knife is done.
steps.leadIn: Mise — set the station (no heat, ~2 min).

steps.text: **Mise — fill the bowls (no heat, ~8 min).** Work the map above; line bowls up ① → ④. **Reset before ignition:** dump garbage bowl, wash knife & board, wipe counter.
steps.leadIn: Mise — fill the bowls (no heat, ~8 min).

steps.text: **Preheat — MEDIUM-HIGH, empty stainless pan, 2–3 min.** Water-drop test: bead-and-skitter. Add the olive oil, wait for a full shimmer. *Dead minute: fill the sink with hot soapy water.*
steps.leadIn: Preheat — MEDIUM-HIGH, empty stainless pan, 2–3 min.

steps.text: **Brown the turkey — stay on MEDIUM-HIGH, ~5–6 min.** Add the turkey and press it into one flat layer with the spoon — then **don't touch for 3–4 min**. You want a deep brown crust underneath (that's fond forming — flavor, not burning). Then crumble into bite-size pieces and cook 2 min more. Done when: no pink, brown crusty bits on the pan bottom.
steps.leadIn: Brown the turkey — stay on MEDIUM-HIGH, ~5–6 min.

steps.text: **Aromatics — drop to MEDIUM, ~3–4 min.** Onion into the turkey, stir until it softens and picks up color. Garlic + the spice bowl in, stir 30–60 sec until fragrant — not brown.
steps.leadIn: Aromatics — drop to MEDIUM, ~3–4 min.

steps.text: **Tomatoes — stay on MEDIUM to a bubble, then MEDIUM-LOW, 15 min.** Pour in bowl ③, scrape the fond up off the bottom (it dissolves into the sauce). Lazy simmer, lid off, stirring occasionally, until it thickens to spoon-track. *Dead minutes: wash the board & spoon rest, set out meal-prep containers.*
steps.leadIn: Tomatoes — stay on MEDIUM to a bubble, then MEDIUM-LOW, 15 min.

steps.text: **Pasta in — stay on MEDIUM-LOW, ~2 min.** Fold the cooked pasta in with a splash of water to loosen; toss until the pasta is hot and glossed with sauce.
steps.leadIn: Pasta in — stay on MEDIUM-LOW, ~2 min.

steps.text: **Balance — OFF HEAT.** Taste. Flat? A small splash of balsamic and a grind of pepper — never salt; the jar already brought it.
steps.leadIn: Balance — OFF HEAT.

steps.text: **Plate.** Shallow bowl, mound high in the center. One dollop (2 tbsp) ricotta on top — don't stir it in, let it melt streaky. Parsley from height, wipe the rim. Remaining 3 portions into containers (fridge 3–4 days; the sauce alone also freezes well).
steps.leadIn: Plate.

title: Mediterranean Lentil Soup (batch — plant-protein lunches)
ingredients: 1 large onion + 2 carrots + 3 celery stalks, diced small (or bell pepper + extra onion)
2 tsp cumin · 1 tsp cinnamon · plenty of black pepper — no salt
4 cups water + 4 cups low-sodium vegetable broth
To serve: Greek yogurt dollop, extra lemon

steps.text: Rinse lentils until water runs clear.
Sweat onion/carrot/celery in oil over medium-high, 6–7 min (skill: aromatics without burning).
Stir in garlic, cumin, cinnamon — 60 seconds until fragrant. Add lentils, toast 1–2 min.
Add liquid + lemon juice; boil, then simmer low **30–45 min** until lentils are tender.
Stir in kale to wilt. Taste: brighten with more lemon + pepper, not salt.

title: The Margarita — Precision Spec 🍸
time: ~8 min active (+ syrup made ahead, + ≥10 min glass chill)
source: [Cointreau — the original Margarita](https://www.cointreau.com/us/en/cocktails/margarita), tuned to the modern 2:¾:¾:¼ balanced spec

bowls.name: The tin, liquids only — NO ice yet
bowls.arrowText: → built in the small tin at step 3, cheapest first
items: ¼ oz (7.5 ml) simple syrup, cold
¾ oz (22 ml) fresh lime juice — squeezed 1–4 h ahead if you can (detail #1)
¾ oz (22 ml) Cointreau
2 oz (60 ml) blanco tequila

bowls.name: Shaking ice
bowls.arrowText: → large tin at step 5, only after the straw-taste
items: ice to fill the large tin ⅔ full — 5–6 standard cubes or 2 big cubes
waits in the freezer until the moment of the shake, never sitting out melting

stationExtras.label: Glass station
stationExtras.arrowText: prepped at step 1, poured at step 7
items: rocks glass → freezer ≥10 min
fresh serving ice for the pour, biggest cubes you have — separate from the shaking ice
optional half-rim — 1 tsp coarse/kosher salt on the small plate + a spare lime wedge
garnish — 1 thin lime wheel, cut during step 1's dead minutes

stationExtras.label: Made ahead — simple syrup
items: 100 g sugar + 100 g water in the small pan over low heat
stir just until fully clear (~3 min), never boil — boiling evaporates water and silently changes the 1-to-1 ratio
cool completely, jar, fridge ~2–3 weeks
yield ~150 ml ≈ 20 margaritas' worth

steps.text: **Chill the glass (freezer, ≥10 min).** ⏱ *Dead minutes — use them:* roll limes hard under your palm (bursts juice vesicles, +20% yield), halve, squeeze ~1–1½ limes, pick out seeds. Cut one thin center wheel for garnish. Ideally this happened 1–4 h ago.
steps.leadIn: Chill the glass (freezer, ≥10 min).

steps.text: **(If rimming) Salt the HALF rim now, on the empty cold glass.** Wedge-wipe the *outside* of half the rim, roll that edge through the salt plate. Outside only — salt inside the rim falls in and you can't undo it. Return glass to freezer.
steps.leadIn: (If rimming) Salt the HALF rim now, on the empty cold glass.

steps.text: **Build the liquids in the small tin, cheapest first:** syrup ¼ oz → lime ¾ oz → Cointreau ¾ oz → tequila 2 oz. (Cheap-first habit: a mis-measure gets dumped before the expensive pour.) Read the jigger at eye level; a ¼-oz miss is a different drink.
steps.leadIn: Build the liquids in the small tin, cheapest first:

steps.text: **Straw-taste the raw build.** Dip a straw, finger over the top, taste. It should read too strong and too intense — the shake's job is to fix exactly that. This is calibration: remember this taste to compare post-shake.
steps.leadIn: Straw-taste the raw build.

steps.text: **Ice the large tin ⅔ full, seal the tins at a slight angle, burp-tap to lock.** Small tin on top. Grip both ends.
steps.leadIn: Ice the large tin ⅔ full, seal the tins at a slight angle, burp-tap to lock.

steps.text: **SHAKE — hard, 12 seconds on a phone timer.** Not a rock, a piston: the ice should slam both ends of the tin. By ~12 s the drink hits thermal equilibrium (–5 to –8 °C, ~25% dilution) and more shaking changes almost nothing — vigor matters, duration past 12–15 s doesn't. The big tin will frost and hurt to hold. That's done.
steps.leadIn: SHAKE — hard, 12 seconds on a phone timer.

steps.text: **Crack the seal (heel of hand where the tins meet), Hawthorne-strain into the chilled glass over FRESH ice.** Never the shaking ice — it's spent, cracked, and fast-melting; it would blow past the 25% dilution target in minutes.
steps.leadIn: Crack the seal (heel of hand where the tins meet), Hawthorne-strain into the chilled glass over FRESH ice.

steps.text: **Balance check (the skill rep):** straw-taste what's left in the tin. Too tart → next time +¼ oz syrup. Too sweet → +¼ oz lime. Flabby/watery → shake was too long or ice sat out. Log the verdict.
steps.leadIn: Balance check (the skill rep):

steps.text: **Plate.** Rocks glass on a coaster, salt-rim (if used) facing away from you so you choose salt sip-by-sip. Lime wheel perched on the clean side of the rim. Wipe any drips off the glass wall. **Tall glass of water alongside — always.** Sip at the 0-minute and 10-minute mark and notice the drink change as the big cubes slowly open it up.
steps.leadIn: Plate.

title: The Cherry-Lime Rickey — Zero-Proof Precision Spec 🍸
time: ~3 min active (+ glass & bottles fridge-cold ahead)
source: classic soda-fountain lime rickey (lime + soda, tart-forward), cherry soda as the metered sweet element

bowls.name: Serving ice
bowls.arrowText: → into the collins glass at step 1, before anything else
items: ice to fill the glass to the rim — the biggest cubes you have
waits in the freezer until the moment of the pour, never sitting out melting

bowls.name: The pour, liquids only
bowls.arrowText: → built straight in the glass at step 2, lime first
items: ½ oz (15 ml) fresh lime juice — one lime, rolled hard before squeezing
3 oz (90 ml) black cherry soda, fridge-cold
3 oz (90 ml) plain soda water, fridge-cold

stationExtras.label: Glass station
stationExtras.arrowText: prepped at step 1, garnished at step 4
items: collins or highball glass → freezer ≥10 min
garnish — 1 lime wheel, cut while the glass chills
1 cocktail cherry, dropped so it sinks

steps.text: **Pull the cold glass and fill it with ice to the rim.** A half-filled glass melts twice as fast — the ice is insulation, not decoration. Cut the lime wheel now, in the dead seconds.
steps.leadIn: Pull the cold glass and fill it with ice to the rim.

steps.text: **Build in the glass, lime first:** ½ oz lime → 3 oz cherry soda → 3 oz soda water. Lime first means you can straw-taste and correct before the bubbles are in. Pour the sodas down the bar spoon to keep the carbonation.
steps.leadIn: Build in the glass, lime first:

steps.text: **One gentle stir — bottom to top, once.** Carbonation is an ingredient; every extra stir spends some. If it reads sweet-first, add another ¼ oz lime — a rickey is tart-forward or it is just soda.
steps.leadIn: One gentle stir — bottom to top, once.

steps.text: **Plate.** Lime wheel on the rim, cherry dropped to the bottom. Wipe the glass wall, coaster underneath. Sip it while it is loud — a rickey is at its best in the first five minutes.
steps.leadIn: Plate.
